newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stops poisoning seagulls off Cape Cod coast.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stops poisoning seagulls off Cape Cod coast.

text.p: The U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service has halted poisoning seagulls at a wildlife refuge off the coast of Cape Cod in Massachusetts in response to public outrage over the culling method.
Ronald Lambertson, regional director of the federal agency, gave Sen. Ted Kennedy the news in a letter that was released to the media late on Friday.

"Many citizens on Cape Cod were disturbed greatly by our gull poisoning actions in 1996 ... the Service has decided that gull poisoning in 1997 is cancelled," Lambertson wrote the Democratic senator from Massachusetts.

The Service poisoned seagulls as part of a four-year programme to protect the roseate tern and piping plover, two endangered species that gulls were crowding out on the Monomoy National Wildlife Refuge.

But public outrage has forced the Service to use its old method of killing gulls -- they will shoot them. The old method "did not generate significant public concern or controversy," Lamberston told Kennedy.
Kennedy commended the Service in a statement noting the poisoning programme "jeopardized the thriving tourism that is the heart of our Cape Cod economy."
